title: Uttara-vibhaga. Lahari 11. The Sending of Wild Elephants at the Request of Shah Shuja and the Giving of Hari-nama to Two Wild Tigers
html:
A song in glory of Shyamananda; for the sake of the festivals Rasika constantly travels with his companions, serving the guru, Krishna and the sadhus; kings and subjects vie with one another to invite him, everywhere the eight siddhis and the nine treasures are with him, and he floods every land with love for Krishna; wicked people tell the Padishah of the great mahanta of Orissa who gives Hari-nama to the forest elephants and with whom Jagannatha converses, and Shah Shuja sends a khoja with a thousand horses and elephants to Gopivallabhapur to demand a miracle: let Rasika by his command bring elephants out of the forest; the Hindu community is alarmed, but Rasika answers with a smile that he knows no tricks, his Master is Krishna, and let the khoja keep the yavanas away while the twelve-day festival lasts and make his preparations; the khoja builds an enclosure, and at night, at Rasika's command, the elephant Gopala Dasa leads fourteen forest elephants into it; the khoja falls at Rasika's feet and acknowledges him as Ishvara, the elephants are taken to the Padishah, and the yavanas acknowledge Rasika as Narayana; in Varahabhumi the companions, losing their way at night, enter a dense forest where two tigers block the path; Rasika steps forward and gives them Hari-nama, and the tigers, bowing, lead everyone out of the forest to a village; people gather to see this, and Rasika bids his companions keep his manifestations secret; the author glorifies Rasika, who gave prema-bhakti to all of Utkala

The eleventh lahari.

Raga Narayani-gauda.1
Ghosha: "My Krishna, treasury of virtues,
refuge of the helpless, the utmost limit of mercy."

1Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the treasury of compassion,
whose wealth [and] life is Rasikendra-chudamani!

2For the sake of the festivals Sri Rasikendra-chandra
always wanders over the earth; with him is a host of Krishna's devotees.2

3He constantly serves the guru, Krishna and the sadhus;
in great bliss he always goes from town to town.

4Kings [and] subjects, vying with one another [to] serve the sadhus,
invite Rasika and take [him to their homes].3

5Sending messengers ten or twenty days ahead
[and] watching for where Prabhu will arrive,

6with their whole families they go joyfully for darshan;
falling at [his] feet, they bring [him], begging him to come.4

7He fulfils the desires of all;
Prabhu wanders in [all] four directions for the sake of living beings.

8Whatever music [and] poetry there is on earth —
all of it always abides with Rasika.

9Wherever Rasikendra-mani stays,
the eight siddhis [and] the nine treasures are present of themselves.

10One who has not even a ser of rice in his house —
as soon as [Rasika] arrives, the eight siddhis at once supply [everything].5

11In the bliss of sankirtana Sri Rasika-chudamani
always himself sings sankirtana [and] dances.

12The eight sattvika [bhavas] appear on his holy body;
with the streams from his eyes [everything] around is drenched.

13How [lovely] the movement of his dance [and] his poses, how [lovely] his gentle smile!
How [sweet] the speech of his holy mouth always is!

14With a special glance he won over all the pilgrims;
he flooded every land, one after another, with love for Krishna.6

15At this time wicked people say to the Padishah:
"There is a very great mahanta in the land of Orissa.

16He gives Hari-nama to the forest elephants;
Jagannatha speaks with him — [this is] certain."7

17Hearing [this], the Padishah says, looking at the khoja:
"Go and tell Rasika: let him catch elephants [and] give [them to us].

18The forest elephants are his servants.
Ask humbly; do not speak harsh words."8

19Hearing [this], the evil-minded khoja quickly set out,
taking with him a thousand horses [and] elephants.

20He arrived in the vicinity of Sri Gopivallabhapur
[and] sent eminent people to Prabhu.

21They submitted to Sri Rasika:
"This is why Shah Shuja has sent me:

22[so that] he may grant me this miracle —
by his command bring elephants out of the forest.

23When ten or twenty elephants come at [his] command,
[we] will surely acknowledge him as Ishvara."9

24[This] reached the whole Hindu community there;
deeming [it] a very great misfortune, they all go [to Rasika].10

25All made it known at Rasika's feet;
with a gentle smile on his face he says to all:

26"I know nothing of tricks [and] shows;
with my whole being, my Master is Lord Krishna.11

27When Lord Krishna shows me mercy,
then the matter will be accomplished — tell the khoja.

28The twelve-day great festival every year
I celebrate with great joy in Sri Gopivallabhapur.

29As long as I am celebrating the festival here,
let not a single one of the yavanas come.

30Tell him: staying at a distance, let him make his preparations;
Krishna will give the elephants if [he] takes pains."12

31All went and told [this] to the evil-minded khoja;
hearing it, he joyfully made many obeisances.13

32On [all] four sides he laid the foundation of a wall;
inside he carefully placed bananas, rice and so on.

33He left there only one entrance with gate-leaves;
and he put his faith in Rasika's words.

34At this time [Rasika] began the festival;
that [very] elephant, Gopala Dasa, came and entered.14

35At night he bowed down to Rasika;
before the elephant Rasika-shekhara spoke:

36"Listen, listen, dear one, maddened best of elephants!
The king of the yavanas has sent servants.

37He has wished to see my miracle:
[that] ten or twenty elephants be brought [and] given [to him] before his eyes.

38At my command, dear one, do one task:
bring ten or twenty elephants [and] put [them] into the enclosure.

39You yourself stay behind, do not go in through the entrance;
show me this very miracle."15

40Receiving the command, the maddened Gopala Dasa quickly went;
in the forest he entered among the elephants.

41The king of elephants, leading the elephants along with him,
brings them inside the enclosure.

42At the entrance he himself turned back [and] went off into the forest;
fourteen elephants went into the enclosure.16

43The servants closed the gate-leaves of the entrance;
seeing [this], that evil-minded yavana was amazed.

44Seeing Rasika's greatness, he quickly came;
falling down like a rod, the khoja falls at [his] feet.

45In many ways he offered praise before Rasika;
he firmly acknowledged [him] as Ishvara.

46He quickly told everything to the Padishah;
[he] brought the elephants [and] gave [them] to him before his eyes.

47Seeing all these signs, the yavanas
from that time acknowledged him as Narayana in person.17

48See, then: at Rasika's command
the forest elephants come to Rasika.18

49In the bliss of Krishna Rasika-shekhara wanders;
constantly, absorbed in Krishna, [his] eyes are full of tears.

50From land to land he travels with a happy heart,
overwhelmed by sankirtana, in the happiness of supreme bliss.

51To Varahabhumi Rasikendra once
journeyed, the Prabhu, taking his own people with him.

52His companions are full of [the arts of] music and poetry;
the Prabhu, Achyuta's son, rides in a palanquin.19

53At this time, losing their way, they entered a forest;
the night is dark, clouds cover the sky.

54Leaving the road, all wander from forest to forest;
all went on and entered an impenetrable thicket.

55At this time two tigers blocked the way;
in fear all said to Rasika:

56"Two very fearsome, ferocious tigers
have blocked [the way] ahead — the wicked ones do not let us pass."20

57Putting everyone behind him, the Prabhu went ahead;
going up to the tigers, he began to speak:

58"Listen, listen, you two tigers!
Both of you, give up wicked deeds, give your minds to Krishna.

59From past sins you were born in a wicked race;
if you do not worship Krishna, you will gain toil birth after birth.

60Worship Krishna's lotus feet with firm resolve;
do not trouble any of the sadhus."21

61Hearing Rasika's words, the two tigers
both fell at [his] feet with tearful eyes.

62Placing his hand on [their] heads, he gave the Hari-nama into [their] ears;
hearing the Name, in great bliss they fell at [his] feet.

63Again and again — circumambulation, again — obeisance;
by seeing Rasika they gained divine knowledge.

64Seeing [all] wandering from forest to forest, the two tigers,
clearing the way, go ahead — the two brothers.

65All walk behind, the two in front;
crossing the forest, they came near a village.22

66Morning came; in the village everyone saw [them] —
hundreds of thousands of people come to see the tigers.23

67Rasika gave a command to the two tigers:
"Go, dear ones, go [and] worship Krishna with care."

68Receiving the command, the two bow down;
circumambulating [him], both went off into the forest.

69All the people saw Rasika's manifestation [of power];
all came, together with [the whole] town, for darshan.

70Such is the greatness of Rasikendra-chudamani:
in the forest country he showed mercy to all the people.

71Rasika gave a command to all his companions:
"All of you, keep all these manifestations secret."

72And all the other manifestations he made in the same way —
receiving the command, the companions kept [them] secret.24

73Inviolable is the word of Sri Rasika-chudamani;
his commands are carried out by the best of gods and men.

74He whose commands are carried out by tiger, bear, elephant, serpent,
whose commands are carried out in heaven by Indra, the great king!

75Hearing of [his] greatness, all became stirred;
children [and] the old — all come [and] receive darshan.25

76In all lands the Prabhu gave prema-bhakti;
the poor, the lowly, down to the chandalas, he delivered.

77The utter fools who lived in the forest country —
all became Vaishnavas by the touch of [his] feet.

78Not even with a hundred mouths can [all] his qualities be told;
he flooded the land of Utkala with love for Krishna.

79By his mercy I have made known a little
of the qualities, glory [and] fame of Shyamananda [and] Rasika.26

80[His] pastimes are a boundless sea, known in the world;
all of you, listen to the Rasika-mangala, giving [it your] heart.

81All the pastimes he performed in the circle of the earth,
all the manifestations he made in waves of bliss —

82even speaking with a hundred mouths, they cannot be described;
the Prabhu is an ocean of qualities, a treasury of compassion.

83In brief I have composed [a song] of [his] fair glory;
listen with joy, people of the three worlds.

84Good people [and] scholars, do not hold [my] faults [against me];
setting faults aside, all of you listen with joy.27

85Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the eleventh lahari, called "The Sending of Wild Elephants at the Request of Shah Shuja and the Giving of Hari-nama to Two Wild Tigers."28

Notes

  1. The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("একাদশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. The raga in the 1941 edition is nārānī gauṛā, i.e. Narayani-gauda (Purva, lahari 7, note 1; lahari 10, note 1); the ghosha (refrain) is the same as there and in Uttara, lahari 1, and its translation is repeated. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে সাহা সুজার অনুরোধে বন্যহস্তী প্রেরণ ও বন্যব্যাঘ্রদ্বয়কে হরিনাম-প্রদান-নাম একাদশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (sāhā sujāra anurodhe banyahastī preraṇa o banyabyāghradbaẏake harināma-pradāna). The summary line covers the whole lahari.
  2. "Rasikendra-chudamani" (1) — "the crest-jewel of Rasikendras," Rasika. "Whose wealth [and] life" — yā̃ra dhana prāṇa. "For the sake of the festivals" (2) — mahotsaba-kāraṇe. "A host of Krishna's devotees" — kārṣṇabṛnda; kārṣṇa — "a devotee of Krishna," as in Purva, lahari 1, note 66.
  3. "Serves the guru, Krishna and the sadhus" (3) — guru-kṛṣṇa-sādhusebā. "Vying with one another" (4) — bādābādi haiẏā. The editor's footnote gives the variant sādhusaba ("all the sadhus") for sādhusebā.
  4. "Ten or twenty days ahead" (5) — daśa biśa dina ha'te: in advance. "Will arrive" — bije … āise: bije — respectful for an arrival. "With their whole families" (6) — sabaṃśe. "Begging him to come" — bije karāiẏā.
  5. The eight siddhis and the nine treasures (9) — lahari 8, note 6. "Ser" (10) — sera, a measure of weight (about a kilogram). "As soon as [he] arrives" — bije mātra. "Supply" — milāẏa.
  6. The eight sattvika-bhavas (12) — lahari 6, note 26. "Poses" (13) — bhaṅgi. "With a special glance" (14) — cāhani biśeṣe. "Won over" — baśa kaila.
  7. The Padishah (pātasāha) — here Shah Shuja (21; note 9). "Wicked people say to the Padishah" (15) — pātasāha kahe duṣṭagaṇe: understood as the wicked people speaking to the Padishah (cf. 17). Mahanta — Pashchima, lahari 7, note 37. "Gives Hari-nama to the forest elephants" (16) — cf. the elephant Gopala Dasa (Pashchima, lahari 8, note 34; Uttara, lahari 7, 30–37). "Jagannatha speaks with him" — jagannātha kathā tāhe kahe: cf. Pashchima, lahari 7, note 37. "Certain" — paramāṇa.
  8. Khoja (khojā, Persian khwāja) — a eunuch official in the Padishah's service. "Let him catch … give" (17) — dhari deuna (respectful imperative). "Harsh words" (18) — kubacana.
  9. "Taking with him" (19) — kariẏā saṃhati. "Eminent people" (20) — baṛa baṛa loka. Shah Shuja — the son of Shah Jahan, governor (subahdar) of Bengal in 1639–1660; the author calls him Padishah. In 21b–23 the khoja speaks (through those he sent). "Miracle" (22) — kerāmata (Pashchima, lahari 7, note 41). "Will acknowledge him as Ishvara" (23) — niścaẏa īśbara bali' āniba tā̃hāẏa: āniba, literally "we will bring"; understood as "we will accept [him as] Ishvara (God)"; possibly a misprint for jāniba, "we will know".
  10. "The Hindu community" (24) — hindugoṣṭhī. "Reached" — paśila, literally "entered." "Deeming" — bhāni'.
  11. "Tricks [and] shows" (26) — cāṭaka nāṭaka. "With my whole being" — sarbbātmabhābete. "My Master is Lord Krishna" — mora kṛṣṇa prabhu sbāmī.
  12. "The twelve-day great festival" (28) — duẏādaśa mahotsaba, literally "twelve festivals" or "a festival of twelve [days]": the festival at Gopivallabhapur (lahari 6, note 1). "Of the yavanas" (29) — yabanera gaṇe: Muslims. "Let him make his preparations" (30) — karuna udyama; "takes pains" — karile yatana. Next the khoja builds an enclosure for the elephants.
  13. "Told [this]" (31) — Rasika's answer (26–30) was conveyed to the khoja by the eminent men he had sent (20–21). "Many obeisances" — bahuta praṇāme. "Laid the foundation of a wall" (32) — prācīrera karilā pattane. "Rice" — dhānya, unhusked rice. "Only one entrance with gate-leaves" (33) — eka dbāra kapāṭa mātra rākhila tā̃'ẏa. "And he put his faith" — biśbāsa kaila āra.
  14. "[Rasika] began the festival" (34) — the twelve-day festival at Gopivallabhapur (28–29, note 12); the subject is not named. The elephant Gopala Dasa — Pashchima, lahari 8, note 34; Pashchima, lahari 10; Uttara, lahari 7, 30–37. "Bowed down" (35) — paraṇāma kailā: the elephant bowed down.
  15. "Dear one" (36, 38) — bāpu, an affectionate address. "Maddened" — matta: the usual epithet of an elephant in rut. "The king of the yavanas" — yabanarājana: the Padishah (Shah Shuja; note 9). "Miracle" (37, 39) — kerāmati (note 9). "Enclosure" (38, 41, 42) — kā̃thi: the stockade built by the khoja (32–33). "Do not go in through the entrance" (39) — nā paśibe dbāre.
  16. "In the forest" (40) — 'raṇyete. "Turned back" (42) — bāhuṛi.
  17. "Falling down like a rod" (44) — daṇḍabat haiẏā. "Acknowledged [him] as Ishvara" (45) — īśbara baliẏā se jānila (cf. 23, note 9). "Narayana in person" (47) — sākṣāta nārāẏaṇa: so the yavanas acknowledge Rasika — enthusiastic praise; see lahari 10, note 14 (Rasika is a devotee and associate, a disciple of Shyamananda, not an incarnation); on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.
  18. "At … command" — ājñā paramāṇe.
  19. "Wanders" (49) — biharaẏa. "Absorbed in Krishna" — kṛṣṇābeśe. Varahabhumi (barāhabhūmi, 51) — apparently Barabhum (Varahabhum), a forest country north-west of Medinipur (now Purulia district, West Bengal). "Once" — kata dine, lit. "after some time." "Journeyed" — bije kaila. "Full of [the arts of] music and poetry" (52) — saṅgītasāhitye pūrṇa (cf. 8). "Rides in a palanquin" — sukapāle bije (lahari 9, note 6).
  20. "Wander" (54) — bhrami bule. "Impenetrable thicket" — gahana-kānana. "Blocked" (55, 56) — āgulila. "Ferocious" (56) — durācāra.
  21. "Both" (58) — dõhe. "In a wicked race" (59) — duṣṭa kule. "Toil" — śrama, lit. "hard labour, exhaustion." "With firm resolve" (60) — dṛṛhabhābe. "Do not trouble" — nā karibe udbege.
  22. "Placing his hand on [their] heads" (62) — muṇḍe hasta diẏā. 63 — in the 1941 edition ॥ ৬৩ ॥. "Divine knowledge" — dibyajñāna. "Seeing [all] wandering" (64) — bane bane bhramaṇa dekhiẏā: understood as the tigers seeing the travellers wandering. "Clearing the way" — patha karāiẏā. "The two brothers" — dui bhāi: of the tigers. "Came near a village" (65) — haila grāme upasana (= upasanna).
  23. "Morning" — bihāna (the editor glosses "বিহান—সকাল," "morning"). "Hundreds of thousands" — lakṣa lakṣa: hyperbole.
  24. "Dear ones" (67) — bāpu (note 15). "Manifestation [of power]" (69, 71, 72) — prakāśa. "Together with [the whole] town" (69) — nagara sahite. "Keep secret" (71) — kara saṅgopane.
  25. "Inviolable" (73) — alaṅghya. "The best of gods and men" — suranaradebamaṇi, lit. "the jewels [among] suras, men [and] devas." 73–74 — the author's enthusiastic praise; see note 17. "Serpent" (74) — nāga. "Became stirred" (75) — uccāṭana.
  26. "Down to the chandalas" (76) — ācaṇḍāla. "Utter fools" (77) — gaṇḍamūrkha. "Forest country" — banabhūmi (cf. 70: banabhūma). "By his mercy" (79) — tā̃'ra anugrahe: apparently by Rasika's mercy (cf. lahari 10, 67). "Of the qualities, glory [and] fame of Shyamananda [and] Rasika" — śyāmānanda rasikera guṇa yaśaḥ kīrtta; it may also be understood as "of Rasika, [the disciple] of Shyamananda."
  27. "A boundless sea" (80) — apāra-samudra-līlā. "In waves of bliss" (81) — ānanda-kallole. "A treasury of compassion" (82) — karuṇānidhāna. "Of [his] fair glory" (83) — suyaśaḥ. "Do not hold [my] faults [against me]" (84) — doṣa nā laibe; "setting faults aside" — doṣa parihari'. Cf. lahari 9, 73.
  28. The colophon is; the title as in the heading of the lahari. On Shah Shuja — note 9.
